title: How We Made $10M+ Running an Equity Perps Arbitrage Bot
key_claim: Maker-first on HIP-3, hedge on IBKR only after fill; per-market maker/taker param sets; hedge batching by delta accumulation (min 55 / max 400 shares); maxDelta 800 kill-switch; 90 min manual unwind of $120m naked gold shorts cost $1.1m; $32B volume / ~$500k per week at peak.

title: Ran a cross-venue arb bot on Polymarket for 3 months (arb +$8.3k, unhedged residual -$3.2k)
key_claim: Passive-only entries force one-leg-first execution; the unhedged residual lost 38% of gross arb profit; stale-quote adverse selection (fills at stale odds) identified as the dominant loss driver; win rate decayed 50.2->48.3->43.4 monthly as competition arrived.

title: Polymarket Binary Hedging Arbitrage: From Concept to Live Execution
key_claim: Both legs submitted concurrently with leg2 price reverse-computed as SUM_TARGET - leg1Price so pair edge is locked at submission; unhedged Leg 1 managed with FLOOR_PRICE (0.05), EARLY_TAKE_PROFIT, last-minute STOP_LOSS; cancel leg 2 before closing leg 1; on-chain order confirm loop with ORDER_TIMEOUT_S and cancel/retry.

title: Crypto Spot-Futures Arbitrage in Practice: Lessons Learned from Theory to Reality
key_claim: Six pitfalls: (1) single-leg risk -> immediate market-order rollback of filled leg + cooldown; (2) market orders can be rejected too -> limit-first with market fallback, 3 retries; (3) ticker data on illiquid legs lags 0.1-0.5% normal / 1-3% volatile -> price off depth order-book, not last trade; (4) re-verify spread with fresh books right before sending; (5) clear residual positions before new entries; (6) P&L must use actual AvgPrice of fills, not frozen entry price.

title: Hyperliquid Funding Rate Arbitrage vs Binance & Bybit
key_claim: Leg HL maker first (thinner book), then immediately hit CEX taker after HL confirms; cap by only legging instruments with sub-0.5% bid-ask on both venues; size legs so 40% adverse move doesn't liquidate (2.5x effective); 8h-rolling-average spread must clear 3-4x round-trip fee before entry; post-only both entries ~0.08% round-trip; 14-day time-in-trade cap; pre-positioned USDC float on both venues because bridge is 15-40 min.

title: Funding Rate Arb: Hyperliquid vs Binance and Bybit Compared
key_claim: Break-even spread at taker/taker ~4.5 bps per 8h window; anything under 8 bps marginal unless one leg is passive; target 10 bps minimum before opening; BTC +4-8 bps/8h avg spread, ETH 15-20 bps spikes mean-reverting in 24-48h; SOL 10-18 bps persistent; HL maker rebate -0.2bps; residual delta between fills is your entry basis, log it.

title: Hyperliquid vs CEXs: Is Perp Arbitrage Still Worth It After Fees, Funding, and Slippage?
key_claim: Maker both legs round-trip ~0.07%, forced taker one side 0.13-0.20%; break-even funding spread ~1.3 bps/8h at maker with 7d hold; slippage: HL ~5bps at $100k, ~12bps at $500k, ~28bps at $1m (TWAP needed); rule: clip <0.5% of 24h volume, split 3-5 child orders 30-60s apart; post-only gives 2-3bps price improvement on HL ~60% of attempts; desks enter 10-15 min before funding window; never hold through a funding sign-flip, unwind within 60s of reversal.

title: XEMM: Cross-Exchange Market Making, Pacifica (maker) / Hyperliquid (taker)
key_claim: Maker price computed from the taker hedge price: price = (HL_bid*(1-taker_fee))/(1+maker_fee+profit_rate); profit_rate_bps 15 as safety margin over fees+slippage+latency; cancel if profit deviates +/-3 bps; auto-cancel stale maker orders at 60s; 4-layer fill detection (WS fill feed + 500ms REST poll + position monitor ground truth + pre-cancel check) deduplicated so exactly one hedge per fill; hedge on WS with REST fallback; maker placement halts in Reconciling state if a hedge event can't be queued.

title: Why Prediction-Market Arbitrage Disappears After Fees, Slippage, and Fill Risk
key_claim: Second-leg move risk is nonlinear: a 1-cent move on a 100-share pair flipped +$0.60 edge into -$0.40; partial fill splits the trade into matched bundle (70) + unmatched directional (30) which must be tracked and sized separately; maker vs taker compared on expected completed bundles, not fee; before entry, pre-compute the unwind loss (cross spread + one-two tick move + fee) and size position off that, not off gross edge.

title: Funding Arb — Risk Inventory (alexanderlmoran/funding-arb-bot)
key_claim: Partial fill rule: executor retries missing leg 3x within 60s, then closes the filled leg to restore flat (re-flatten cost ~0.15% of the gap, accepted); maker-first executor with 60s timeout then taker fallback; hard +1% basis-drift kill per position; kill-switch hierarchy soft-pause / hard-close / full-halt with specific triggers; executor refuses to trade if last funding read >2min old; exit when funding <=0 for 2 consecutive reads; maker fill rate <50% for a month = upgrade colocation or accept taker regime.

title: Funding Arb — Edges Ranked by $/Day Impact
key_claim: Maker-only execution drops round-trip cost 60-80% but 'if the maker order fills, price is moving against you' — adverse selection stated as the bottleneck, partial fills leave delta-exposed; maker fill reliability is the bottleneck of funding-snipe (Edge 5); alt funding dispersion: HL 0.05-0.15%/hr vs Bybit 0.01%/8h on alts; venue-cap 30% at HL; measure maker fill rate monthly.

title: Quoting the Touch Does Not Pay Its Adverse Selection (Bybit/Binance/Hyperliquid)
key_claim: Back-of-queue touch quoter across 125.8M fills: net entry markout at 10s is -0.84bp Bybit, -0.39bp Binance, -0.46bp Hyperliquid before fees — captured half-spread does not cover post-fill drift on any venue; deeper levels lose less per fill (-0.72 at touch vs -0.33bp at 5th level) but fill at only 12% of touch rate; queue position matters ~0.8bp on HL (front-of-queue +0.32bp vs average -0.48bp).

title: Funding rate arbitrage scanner: Hyperliquid, Lighter, Aster gaps net of fees
key_claim: 237 tokens on 2+ DEXs; only 3 of 8 tokens with >=$10M OI on both legs covered four taker fills over the last 7 days; markets below $1M OI hidden because 'a $10k position moves them, and spread plus slippage exceed the funding'; below $10M OI the net is an upper bound; this-hour gap 'usually gone within two' hours.
